# Remediation mapping

| Scanner | Check | Resource | Articles | Generated | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| prowler | ec2_ebs_default_encryption | 000000000000 | NIS2 Art.21(2)(h), DORA Art.9, ISO27001:2022 A.8.24 | terraform/ebs_default_encryption__000000000000_us-east-1.tf | remediated |  |
| prowler | ec2_networkacl_allow_ingress_any_port | acl-default | NIS2 Art.21(2)(i), NIS2 Art.21(2)(g), DORA Art.9, ISO27001:2022 A.8.20, ISO27001:2022 A.8.22 |  | guidance only | No code is generated on purpose. Network ACLs are stateless and cover whole subnets, so a wrong change drops traffic at once and can lock out users. Terraform also cannot edit an entry it does not manage. Review the entries (aws ec2 describe-network-acls), then replace the open allow entry with your trusted range: aws ec2 replace-network-acl-entry --network-acl-id ACL --ingress --rule-number N --protocol tcp --port-range From=443,To=443 --cidr-block TRUSTED_CIDR --rule-action allow. Keep return traffic (ephemeral ports 1024-65535) allowed. The default network ACL of a new VPC allows everything by design; security groups are the main control. |
| prowler | ec2_networkacl_allow_ingress_tcp_port_22 | acl-default | NIS2 Art.21(2)(i), NIS2 Art.21(2)(g), DORA Art.9, ISO27001:2022 A.8.20, ISO27001:2022 A.8.22 |  | guidance only | No code is generated on purpose. Network ACLs are stateless and cover whole subnets, so a wrong change drops traffic at once and can lock out admins. Terraform also cannot edit an entry it does not manage. Replace the open entry with your admin range: aws ec2 replace-network-acl-entry --network-acl-id ACL --ingress --rule-number N --protocol tcp --port-range From=22,To=22 --cidr-block ADMIN_CIDR --rule-action allow. Test access from the admin range before you remove the old entry. |
| prowler | ec2_networkacl_allow_ingress_tcp_port_3389 | acl-default | NIS2 Art.21(2)(i), NIS2 Art.21(2)(g), DORA Art.9, ISO27001:2022 A.8.20, ISO27001:2022 A.8.22 |  | guidance only | No code is generated on purpose. Network ACLs are stateless and cover whole subnets, so a wrong change drops traffic at once and can lock out admins. Terraform also cannot edit an entry it does not manage. Replace the open entry with your admin range: aws ec2 replace-network-acl-entry --network-acl-id ACL --ingress --rule-number N --protocol tcp --port-range From=3389,To=3389 --cidr-block ADMIN_CIDR --rule-action allow. Test access from the admin range before you remove the old entry. |
| prowler | eks_cluster_private_nodes_enabled | nr-eks | NIS2 Art.21(2)(i), NIS2 Art.21(2)(g), DORA Art.9, ISO27001:2022 A.8.20 |  | guidance only | No safe drop-in code exists because the cluster is not in your Terraform state. Enable endpoint_private_access on the existing aws_eks_cluster vpc_config, or run: aws eks update-cluster-config --name CLUSTER --resources-vpc-config endpointPrivateAccess=true,endpointPublicAccess=CURRENT_VALUE. Keep endpointPublicAccess at its current value, or API access may be lost. This check only needs private access to be on. Closing the public endpoint is a separate step (eks_cluster_not_publicly_accessible). |
